policy: Every occurrence is reviewed in its complete source verse. Confirmed active records were separately approved; proposed records remain inactive.

records.reason: Here prevent means to go before the believers who have died; it does not mean to stop them.
records.sourceText: For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.

records.reason: The speakers deny that disaster will overtake or meet them; modern prevent would reverse the claim.
records.sourceText: All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.

records.reason: The knees receive the newborn Job; they are not obstructing him.
records.sourceText: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?

records.reason: God goes before the speaker in mercy; modern prevent would suggest obstruction.
records.sourceText: The God of my mercy shall prevent me: God shall let me see my desire upon mine enemies.

records.reason: The prayer asks mercy to come quickly to meet the people, not to hinder them.
records.sourceText: O remember not against us former iniquities: let thy tender mercies speedily prevent us: for we are brought very low.

records.reason: The morning prayer comes before God; it does not hinder God.
records.sourceText: But unto thee have I cried, O LORD; and in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee.

records.expected: Mine eyes prevent the night watches
records.proposedReplacement: Mine eyes are awake before the night watches
records.reason: The speaker is awake before the appointed night watches in order to meditate.
records.sourceText: Mine eyes prevent the night watches, that I might meditate in thy word.

records.reason: The snares of death confronted or came upon the speaker; they did not protect him from death.
records.sourceText: The sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;

records.reason: The enemies confronted the speaker in his calamity; the LORD then sustained him.
records.sourceText: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.

records.expected: prevented with their bread him that fled
records.proposedReplacement: met him that fled with their bread
records.reason: The inhabitants meet the fugitive with provisions; modern prevent would reverse the hospitable action.
records.sourceText: The inhabitants of the land of Tema brought water to him that was thirsty, they prevented with their bread him that fled.

records.expected: the days of affliction prevented me
records.proposedReplacement: the days of affliction came upon me
records.reason: The days of affliction came upon Job; they did not stop him from another action.
records.sourceText: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

records.expected: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him?
records.proposedReplacement: Who hath first given to me, that I should repay him?
records.reason: The question denies that anyone gave to God first and thereby placed God in debt.
records.sourceText: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay him? whatsoever is under the whole heaven is mine.

records.proposedReplacement: Jesus spoke first to him, saying
records.reason: Jesus addresses Peter before Peter raises the question; Jesus does not obstruct him.
records.sourceText: He saith, Yes. And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying, What thinkest thou Simon of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute of their own children or of strangers

records.reason: The snares of death confronted or came upon the speaker; they did not protect him from death.
records.sourceText: The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me.

records.reason: The enemies confronted the speaker in his calamity; the LORD then sustained him.
records.sourceText: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.

records.expected: I prevented the dawning of the morning
records.proposedReplacement: I rose before the dawning of the morning
records.reason: The speaker rises and cries before dawn; prevent marks earlier time.
records.sourceText: I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word.

records.reason: Conversation refers to the believer’s whole manner of life, not only speech.
records.sourceText: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;

records.reason: The inherited pattern being described is a way of life, not merely spoken conversation.
records.sourceText: Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers;

records.reason: The surrounding contrast with good works shows that conversation means visible conduct.
records.sourceText: Having your conversation honest among the Gentiles: that, whereas they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they shall behold, glorify God in the day of visitation.

records.reason: The wives’ conduct, even without a spoken word, is what may win the husbands.
records.sourceText: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;

records.reason: What is observed is chaste conduct, not a verbal exchange.
records.sourceText: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.

records.reason: The accusers observe and misrepresent Christian conduct, not a single conversation.
records.sourceText: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.

records.reason: Conversation is one category of Timothy’s example alongside speech, love, faith and purity, so it means conduct.
records.sourceText: Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.

records.expected: we have had our conversation in the world
records.proposedReplacement: we have conducted ourselves in the world
records.reason: The testimony concerns how Paul and his companions behaved in the world.
records.sourceText: For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.

records.reason: Lot is distressed by the wicked people’s conduct, not by their dialogue.
records.sourceText: And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:

records.reason: The call concerns a holy manner of life and godliness.
records.sourceText: Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness,

records.expected: we all had our conversation in times past
records.proposedReplacement: we all lived in times past
records.reason: The clause describes the former life governed by fleshly desires.
records.sourceText: Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others.

records.reason: The old self belongs to the former way of life, not to former speech.
records.sourceText: That ye put off concerning the former conversation the old man, which is corrupt according to the deceitful lusts;

records.reason: Paul refers to his former manner of life in Judaism and the actions that followed.
records.sourceText: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:

records.reason: The instruction concerns a life free from covetousness and content with present provision.
records.sourceText: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

records.reason: Readers are told to consider the outcome of their leaders’ way of life.
records.sourceText: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

records.reason: Wisdom is to be demonstrated through works arising from good conduct.
records.sourceText: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.

records.reason: The command concerns living in a manner worthy of the gospel and standing together.
records.sourceText: Only let your conversation be as it becometh the gospel of Christ: that whether I come and see you, or else be absent, I may hear of your affairs, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel;

records.reason: This occurrence is civic identity in heaven, not speech or merely general conduct; it must not share the bulk conduct rule.
records.sourceText: For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:

records.reason: The phrase describes the upright person’s way of living.
records.sourceText: The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, and to slay such as be of upright conversation.

records.reason: The person orders his way of life rightly; the statement is not about arranging speech.
records.sourceText: Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.

records.reason: Quick contrasts directly with dead and therefore means living.
records.sourceText: Who shall give account to him that is ready to judge the quick and the dead.

records.reason: Quick contrasts directly with dead and therefore means living.
records.sourceText: I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom;

records.reason: Quick contrasts directly with dead and therefore means living.
records.sourceText: And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead.

records.reason: Quick describes the word of God as living, not merely fast.
records.sourceText: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

records.expected: And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the LORD
records.proposedReplacement: And he will delight in the fear of the LORD
records.reason: The complete clause was reviewed against the Hebrew sense and close English controls; delight preserves the positive orientation toward fearing the LORD without treating quick as speed.
records.activeReason: Quick understanding is no longer transparent and can imply mental speed. The Hebrew uses a smell/delight idiom; the close NKJV comparison and lexical note support delight while preserving the verse’s focus on reverence for the LORD.
records.sourceText: And shall make him of quick understanding in the fear of the LORD: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears:

records.reason: The complete diagnostic phrase was reviewed against the Hebrew and close English controls; raw flesh preserves the visible sign without the obsolete quick.
records.activeReason: Quick means living here, not fast. The Hebrew phrase denotes exposed or raw living tissue; raw flesh states the sign without assigning a modern diagnosis.
records.sourceText: And the priest shall see him: and, behold, if the rising be white in the skin, and it have turned the hair white, and there be quick raw flesh in the rising;

records.reason: The complete diagnostic phrase was reviewed against the Hebrew and close English controls; raw flesh of the burn preserves both the sign and its burn context.
records.activeReason: Quick describes living or raw tissue, while that burneth obscures the Hebrew relationship to the burn. This wording clarifies the observable sign without inventing a diagnosis.
records.sourceText: ¶ Or if there be any flesh, in the skin whereof there is a hot burning, and the quick flesh that burneth have a white bright spot, somewhat reddish, or white;

records.expected: go down quick into the pit
records.proposedReplacement: go down alive into the pit
records.reason: Quick means alive as the people descend, not rapidly.
records.sourceText: But if the LORD make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain unto them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the LORD.

records.reason: Quick means alive at the time of descent, not rapidly.
records.sourceText: Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness is in their dwellings, and among them.

records.reason: Quick means alive when swallowed, not rapidly.
records.sourceText: Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:
